title: A Separation between Full-Rank PVM and Assumption-free Self-Testing
abstract: We construct a nonlocal game that self-tests a maximally entangled qubit strategy among pure full-Schmidt-rank projective strategies, but admits an inequivalent optimum using one nonprojective measurement. This resolves a conjecture of Baptista et al. on imposing full rank and projectivity simultaneously. The construction combines CHSH with an auxiliary game $G$ that forces deterministic answers under these assumptions and admits a trine POVM optimum without them. We classify the optimal correlations of $G$ as a line segment parametrized by the tracial states of $\mathbb{C}\oplus M_2(\mathbb{C})$. Projectivity on the state support removes the matrix summand, whereas projective dilations with nonzero nonabort probability have a nontracial local state whose zero left ideal is not two-sided. Finally, a family in local dimension six shows that the full-rank PVM self-test is not robust.
summary: This paper rigorously demonstrates that the self-testing of maximally entangled qubit strategies is not robust when restricted only to full-rank Projective Measurements (PVMs). By constructing a specific nonlocal game, the authors show that optimal correlations achievable with nonprojective measurements are fundamentally different from those achievable under the strict PVM assumption.
main_problem: The paper investigates the robustness of self-testing protocols for maximally entangled qubit strategies when restricted to pure, full-Schmidt-rank Projective Measurements (PVMs). It aims to resolve a conjecture regarding the simultaneous imposition of full rank and projectivity.
main_result: The authors prove a separation: an optimal strategy using a nonprojective measurement can be found that does not admit a local dilation to the reference state, demonstrating that the full-rank PVM self-test is not robust.
method: The analysis constructs a nonlocal game $H$ combining CHSH with an auxiliary game $G$. The core method involves comparing the algebraic structure of optimal correlations derived from PVMs versus those from nonprojective measurements, utilizing local dilation concepts.
model_or_system: The study uses qubits ($\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$) and the maximally entangled state $|\Phi^+angle$ within the framework of nonlocal games. The analysis heavily relies on the algebraic structure of optimal correlations, involving $C^*$-algebras like $C \oplus M_2(C)$.
key_observables: The quantum value ($\omega_q(H)$) and classical value ($\omega_c(H)$) of the constructed game $H$; the local dilation error.
important_parameters: The parameter $t \in (0, 1)$ controlling the deviation from the reference state; the specific correlation values like $19/22$ and $71/88$.
main_assumptions: The argument hinges on the algebraic difference between deterministic optima (from projectivity) and trine optima (from nonprojectivity) in the auxiliary game $G$.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the auxiliary game $G$ to establish a discrepancy between its projective and nonprojective optima. It then combines $G$ with the CHSH game to construct $H$, culminating in the proof of the separation theorem showing the non-robustness of the PVM self-test.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical understanding of the limitations of self-testing protocols in quantum information theory, showing that imposing physical constraints (like projectivity) can fundamentally alter the set of achievable correlations.
